reviews.text: Reworking the review as the edits were getting longer. As of present, many of the early issues have been resolved in terms of character creation, a variety of stat bugs, several broken skills and balance issues involving stats stacking when they shouldn't or skills scaling exponentially beyond what was intended. The Talent tree is slowly getting better, but it's still difficult to search for some things in an indirect manner. You pretty much have to type a word of what you want, hope it's in the suggested list and target the specific one in order to locate them, instead of a simple keyword search. Example: You type Health and instead of getting all nodes related to health highlighted, it instead suggests specific stats related to health that you have to select to make those highlight instead. Translations still leave a lot to be desired and the formatting of stats just doesn't work... Things like "Increase Area of Effect(Less) 50%" instead of "Reduces Area of Effect by 50%". I'm assuming this is an issue in how they are handling translations where they are just replacing words in Chinese with English equivalents but ignoring the need to change the format. This tends to result in it being difficult to ascertain what a property really does and whether it's better or worse, or even at times what it even effects. There is also still numerous Chinese text that does not have translations as they should. That all said, they did add an encyclopedia with some explanations about unexplained properties (like finally telling us what Sweep exactly does), but it's still in a very basic form and I suspect will be getting regular updates. Hybrid classes are still missing, and will be for the foreseeable future as they have been removed from their original planned release at launch and added to a future roadmap. You can tell from the store description, the demo and the web that the three hybrid classes were intended to be there at launch, but were pushed back to meet a deadline. This results in bad vibes for the passive web tree if you want to play a build that uses two stats, as you have to invest roughly 10-11 skill points to move from STR, INT or DEX into the dual stat sections of the passive web, which actually holds a lot of powerful talents/passives. Think Path of Exile but they decided to launch without Dualist, Templar or Shadow. Overall, things are moving forward and improving, but there are still numerous bugs, QOL issues and translation struggles. Still at a state that those that enjoy doing trial and error theory crafting and experimentation will probably enjoy themselves, but casual players will probably be turned off from it. If this kind of game interests you, you're an english speaker and don't enjoy a lack of handholding/explanation, I'd recommend adding it to your follow/wishlist and just keeping an eye on it but holding off on pulling the trigger. The core features are there and you can see a good game with lots of depth under the mess but honestly, this just wasn't ready for a 1.0 release and it shows.

5.2补充 天赋过滤和拾取过滤问题已经得到改善，这点还是要好评的。 文本问题还是非常大，尽管官方说接下来会有帮助手册一类的东西，但我仍然感觉不太好。 因为他们做设计的时候感觉根本没有好好写文本。 既然你将技能类型分为了“点击”“普攻”“技能”三个种类，那么为什么要弄那些误导性的词比如“施法速度”“攻击速度”让人误以为攻击系技能吃攻速？ 实际上你游所有技能都吃施法速度。 还有，感觉像是默认所有人都玩过poe2，知道用精魄开光环，游戏里没有任何引导不说，甚至还区分出了sp和魂心值两个称呼，很多新人根本摸不着头脑，我在群里这几天已经见到十几个弄不明白光环的新人了。 真该好好琢磨下你这文本要怎么写，不需要你多严谨，认真点不要误导玩家就可以了。 现在给我的感觉是写这些文本的人根本不玩这个游戏..... 另外还有一点很重要的，我群友玩了五分钟就也被震撼到的——你特么学poe不学他的仓库吗？ 你知不知道你现在的仓库有多难用！！！！！！！！！！ ------------------------------ 虽然你们将它称之为1.0，但在玩家眼里它可能不太配称得上1.0。 因为基础问题有点太多了。 1、天赋过滤问题，明明包含该字段的天赋，但是搜索了对应字段后并不高亮（看了一眼其他评价，原来是要展开选，但是很多字段根本没有对应的可选项，比如游侠搜双持是没有任何高亮，右边展开也没有任何可选项的） 2、物品拾取过滤问题，太简陋了，而且就算不提这个，为什么规则只能有五条？！我不能理解 3、辅助技能太少，很多技能甚至没有几个可以安装的辅助宝石... 4、大量文本描述不明确，没有帮助手册，没有可选查看的详情，以至于玩家想要看自己获得的“增益效果”是什么时，只能进实战看状态栏。 5、补充一下第四点：描述很迷，攻击速度疑似只对平A有效，技能无论攻击技能还是法术技能都吃施法速度（？）我不理解，而且技能面板上只有释放速度，不是攻击速度也不是施法速度。（nm，看了下面板，还真是，技能全部靠施法速度） 我姑且给好评的原因是底子很好，即便是目前这个错漏百出的情况下，也已经值得一玩，就看什么时候改好了。

[h3]About me[/h3] I like odd games. Especially games focused on logic puzzles, stats, character building, theorycrafting, and “number go up” progression. This game fits that niche very well. [h3]What the game does well[/h3] The item stat system is interesting. The skill tree has enough depth to make progression feel meaningful. The skill system is solid, even though it could still be expanded and polished. The story is basically non-existent, but I do not see that as a negative. This game does not need a story. It lives or dies by its systems. To me, this is the first genuinely good attempt at mixing an ARPG with an idle game. If you enjoy idle games and also like games such as Path of Exile or other ARPGs mainly for their character progression, build crafting, and stat scaling, this game is probably for you. [h3]What the game currently does poorly[/h3] EDIT : They added a Lexicon with clear explained interaction of stats, that fixes some confusion. There is no proper extensive tutorial, and several mechanics are not explained at all. Personally, I found that interesting because figuring things out became part of the challenge, but this will not work for everyone. The localization of stats is unfinished. That said, if you have played ARPGs before, most stats can still be deciphered reasonably well. They are not unreadable, just unfinished and sometimes unclear. The game requires you to spend time understanding it. It does not hold your hand. It does not explain everything. It expects you to experiment, read stats, test mechanics, and learn through failure. For me, that is a positive, but for many players it will be frustrating. The game also promised six classes and a more polished product than what was delivered at release. That criticism is fair. However, compared to the previous demo, this version is a clear improvement and, for the price, I think it is acceptable. We are talking about roughly 6 €. I live in Germany and pay that for half a loaf of bread at a bakery if I am lucky. [h3]Current progress[/h3] I have reached Wasteland Stage 130 and am currently crafting, improving my skill setups, and looking for ways to break the game on my next character. [h3]Conclusion[/h3] This is not a polished mainstream ARPG. It is rough, unclear, and unfinished in several areas. But underneath that, there is a genuinely interesting progression system with real potential. If you like idle games, ARPG character progression, stat scaling, and figuring out mechanics yourself, this game is worth the price.

Legends of Wasteland by 清友工作室 is the kind of indie title that immediately signals its ambitions through mood rather than spectacle, placing players into a harsh, desolate setting where survival is not just a mechanic but the central identity of the experience. From the moment the game begins, it establishes a subdued and often oppressive tone, using empty landscapes, worn-down structures, and a restrained visual style to communicate a world that has long since lost its vitality. There is a deliberate slowness to how everything unfolds, encouraging players to observe, adapt, and endure rather than rush forward, which gives the game a distinctive rhythm compared to more action-heavy survival titles. The core gameplay is rooted in familiar survival elements such as gathering resources, crafting tools, and managing limited supplies, but it leans more heavily into atmosphere than complexity. Progression tends to feel incremental, with each small improvement in equipment or knowledge offering a tangible sense of advancement. However, this steady pace can also become a double-edged sword. While it reinforces immersion and makes survival feel meaningful, it can also lead to stretches where the gameplay loop begins to feel repetitive, particularly when new mechanics or variations are introduced sparingly. Players who enjoy methodical, almost meditative gameplay will likely appreciate this design, while others may find it lacking in momentum. Exploration plays a significant role in keeping the experience engaging, as the world is scattered with subtle environmental details that hint at a larger, untold story. Rather than relying on heavy exposition or scripted narrative sequences, the game allows its setting to do most of the storytelling. Abandoned areas, remnants of past activity, and the overall emptiness of the environment all contribute to a quiet sense of mystery. This minimalist approach can be quite effective for players who enjoy piecing together context on their own, though it may feel underdeveloped for those looking for a more structured or character-driven narrative. Interaction with threats, whether environmental or hostile, tends to prioritize tension over depth. Encounters often feel unpredictable enough to keep players cautious, but the underlying systems do not always offer a wide range of strategic options. Combat and survival challenges are serviceable and occasionally intense, yet they rarely evolve in a way that significantly changes how the player approaches the game over time. This results in a consistent experience that maintains its tone well but does not always expand meaningfully on its initial ideas. From a technical standpoint, the game clearly reflects its indie scale. Visuals are modest, with some environments managing to capture a striking sense of desolation while others appear sparse or lacking detail. Animations and interface design can feel a bit rough around the edges, occasionally reminding the player of the game’s limited resources. Despite this, performance is generally stable, and the audio design stands out as one of the stronger elements. Ambient sounds and subtle musical cues do a great deal of work in reinforcing the atmosphere, often carrying moments that might otherwise feel empty. In the end, Legends of Wasteland is a game that succeeds more through its tone and intent than through mechanical innovation or technical polish. It offers a focused survival experience that emphasizes isolation, patience, and environmental storytelling, making it appealing to a niche audience that values immersion over intensity. At the same time, its repetitive structure, limited variety, and rough presentation hold it back from achieving broader appeal. It feels like a solid foundation that could have benefited from further refinement and expansion, but even in its current state, it provides a distinct and occasionally compelling journey for those willing to embrace its slower, more introspective approach. Rating: 7/10

总结一下个人游戏体验，先说一下，本人只深入过战士和射手职业。 战士开荒最适合，只学怒火打击，后面加个爆炎被动去打溅射清图，天赋优先点出朴素战士，等级高了后技能换怒火宣泄，被动带多重施法，清图神技。然后转职和装备优先选叠加狂怒、火伤害（还有命中），饰品火球术点燃,这样深入搭配，开打荒域。 射手天赋点出疾风守护后面点第二宠物，带两个高生命的宠物（天赋第二宠物），衣服一定要有共生（传奇），不然可能活不了，天赋走流血派系，尽可能提高点击频率，连发，撕裂。被动技能带痛苦分享，多重施法。主技能带个瞄准姿态，饰品火球术，叠流血，简单无脑一样可以冲深渊.(射手这种玩法后期上限高一点，当然也很掉帧)。 法师：目前还没深入，改天试试。 最后，设计平衡问题，如我上面所说的攻略，每个职业只有一两个技能好用（能用），能不能重新写一下机制和数值？

like action RPGs, but I usually end up dropping them once the farming starts to feel too repetitive. This game solves that problem by mixing action RPG gameplay with idle mechanics. The repetitive farming is automated, so you can leave the game running and come back later to find that you’ve gained levels, collected materials, or picked up the gear you were farming for. At the same time, it still keeps the fun part of action RPGs: experimenting with different builds. You can focus more on planning skills, gear, and playstyles without constantly worrying about grinding for levels or materials, since most of that happens automatically. That is what made me enjoy the game. It has a good variety of builds, a solid skill tree, and enough depth for players who enjoy designing and testing different setups. It does have some flaws, but for the price, I’d say you’re getting a very solid game. The developers also seem active, listen to feedback, and update the game often with improvements.

"Mixed" I think is a befitting rating. If I could sideways this I probably would, though it's also the case that if I could return it at 2-3 hours (instead of <2) I would probably return it. The concept here I think is great; the issues are in the execution. Pros: Dev has been busy with regular bug fixes Bringing POE skill tree to an incremental game is an interesting notion The array of systems - in theory - provides a lot of options to customize Cons: Balance feels off - the majority of fights are either too easy or too hard and imo it's a bit too hard to find the sweet spot of where progression will be challenging but rewarding. Tooltips/info are a bit lacking at times. The grand skill tree doesn't help when I'm not entirely sure what is/isn't being buffed. Unless you specifically spec into it, the basic 'attack' option feels incredibly weak so maybe I should just idle and not actively play at all? I had played the demo before buying and was sure I was on the cusp of unlocking...something...that brought the game together. But no, it's a game with a bunch of systems that sound cool, but can't really elevate it past its limits. I'll revisit this review at some point in the future if I see a major patch, but as is I spend more time being puzzled/frustrated than engaged. Can't return, but will uninstall.

When I first started off, I began wondering "Why is this mixed rating? This looks to be an incredible game!", but the more I played, the more I realized why it has mixed - and it's actually the correct rating for this. The best way to put this is that it's an Idle Path of Exile. Speaking as someone with 4500 hours in Path of Exile and loves Idlers / Incremental type games, this sounds like a godsend, but it's really not. There are more problems with the game than there is good. The #1, most blatant issue is the game is barely in English, almost like everything was hastily Google Translated or done by someone with no concept of what these words mean in video games. You can get a "good enough of a guess" understanding of most things, but some make no sense at all: "Terrain Damage" is a good example. As far as the game itself, it's trying to do too much while also not doing enough to get you situated. Within the first 2 acts, you're going to have a bunch of mechanics thrown at you immediately, including pets that join you in combat, skill gems, skill gems for your skill gems, gear, guild, shop, crafting (both a forge and items), the skill tree itself which is a rough copy + paste of the Path of Exile tree, difficulty sliders, endless mode, and this is all just within the first 30 minutes. You also absolutely have to hop out at the end of each area to complete the quests to finishing that area, otherwise you're going to fall behind on XP and gold. Then, as I said above about not doing enough to get you situated, some skills require certain weapons to use, but you don't get to choose what you get, the game decides for you. So, if you're a mage and you want a wand, the quest only awards a staff, and the only way to get a wand is if the shop's RNG allows you to roll one, otherwise, you're not going to be able to build your character the way you want to right off the bat. There's a lot to unpack but this game needs far, far, far more time in the oven. This has the potential to be the greatest idle RPG since Melvor, but it's not even close to being ready to be released yet.

一款内容丰富的挂机刷宝游戏。开局有战士、游侠、法师3大职业可选，后续转职还会细分到12个二转职业，均有专属的天赋加成。职业流派多样，技能可以交叉搭配使用，可构筑出更多的战斗风格。多达千个的天赋树节点，除了攻击防护的加成，还有基础属性加成，属性还可以根据橙武要求随时更改。游戏除了经典的故事模式，还有无尽的冒险模式，秘境副本，入侵模式，荒域探索等等，玩法多样。
Chinese centric based idler RPG with what looks to be a huge skill tree. Achievements will take a while as any idler.
